messages:
alex: quick heads-up — noticed weird quota attribution when a customer uses a service account from project-B to call project-A's endpoints. routing ends up charging project-B but telemetry shows project-A latency. anyone else seen this?
priya: ugh. is this the SA being minted in org scope vs project scope? can you paste an example call flow?
alex: yep. flow: customer uses sa key from proj-B -> frontend proxies -> calls internal appeal endpoint on proj-A. header has X-Org and X-Project but we route by key identity.
chen: how are we currently resolving billing attribution? key -> owner project id, then route? that would explain charges on proj-B.
alex: exactly. but our routing policy for latency telemetry uses effective project (where route landed) so dashboards show latency under proj-A.
jamal: security POV: we should never rely on opaque frontend headers for authz. but attribution should follow key provenance for billing.
nora: that split will break product dashboards and quota enforcement. customers will see token usage under one project but errors/latency under another. noisy.
chen: short-term patch: have the proxy inject a routed_project tag so telemetry bridges both sides. add a metric: routed_project!=billing_project -> increment mismatch_counter.
priya: for console UX, we need a clear signal: in Usage page show both "Request origin" and "Served by" with toggles. also show mismatch alerts for org admins.
alex: agree. also need to handle quota checks: should we enforce against billing_project or served_project? current impl enforces served_project quotas which lets billing_project exceed limits but gets billed.
jamal: enforce against billing_project. otherwise denial-of-service surface for tenants. billing_project is the authority for key usage.
chen: technical sticky point: enforcement happens at edge (fast path) where we only have the routing decision. we can look up key->billing_project in the fast path cache but adds a hop. cost to latency? around ~0.5ms if cached.
priya: acceptable if we make it an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers during rollout. default to billing_project enforcement for new signups. document in console.
nora: telemetry: we should emit these tags: billing_project, served_project, key_id, route_variant, canary_flag. sample 10% of requests for full trace then upsample on mismatch.
infra-bot: deploy patch candidate: branch "sa-attrib-fix" queued for staging. CI: 12/12 passing.
alex: nice. can we also add a dashboard widget that surfaces top-10 mismatched pairs last 24h? product wants to triage customers quickly.
chen: will add a metrics endpoint and grafana panel. plan: metric name "sa_attribution_mismatch" labels: billing_project, served_project, reason.
jamal: add a security label for "cross-project-access" to trigger audit log retention for those requests.
priya: rollout plan: 1) telemetry + mismatch counting in staging, 2) console UX showing both project fields (beta), 3) enforcement switch defaulting to billing_project for new orgs, 4) full enforcement migration with migration job to reconcile historical usage.
alex: timeline?
priya: staging telemetry this week, console UX mock by EOD Thu, canary 2% next Tue, ramp 100% in 3 weeks if no regressions.
nora: will add alert: if mismatch_rate > 0.5% for any org for >1h, auto-create ticket in internal queue.
chen: one more thing: service accounts that are shared across many projects will inflate billing_project. we should allow org-level billing override mapping in console.
jamal: and require approval flow for org billing overrides. security + finance sign-off.
alex: ok thanks all. I'll drop sample logs and a short reproducer snippet in the thread.
alex: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SAKEY_B" -H "X-Project: proj-A" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```
alex: logs: ``[edge] key=SAKEY_B owner=proj-B routed=proj-A latency=120ms billed_to=proj-B``
priya: perfect. saves a lot of back-and-forth. tagging @nora for the dashboard bits. :thumbsup:
